text: A project set out to work out how often rivers across Spain and neighbouring parts of southwestern Europe burst their banks and caused serious damage, going back hundreds to thousands of years before gauge measurements began, by reading the bands of mud that had settled on lake bottoms. How did its researchers work out which of those buried bands had been laid down by such an event?
reference_answer: The project (FLOODARC) worked from sediment cores and geochemical and chronological datasets that were already available for the studied Iberian sites: it started with descriptions of those cores, then prepared thin sections and applied a state-of-the-art protocol that combined detailed microfacies analyses with geochemical analyses to identify the flood layers. The flood records it analysed span from the last centuries in the Western Ebro Basin (NE Spain) to the last 26000 years in NW Spain.
notes: Seed 796752 (FLOODARC) taken from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-02; drift check SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocTitle='hydrometeorology' -> 1, unchanged. The answer is composed from report_text.workPerformed: 'The flood reconstruction involved initial sediment core descriptions and thin section preparations to identify flood layers using a state-of-the-art protocol that combined detailed microfacies analyses with geochemical analyses.' Question text was reworded in the fix round to earn term_style=paraphrase: it no longer contains 'flood', 'Western Mediterranean' or 'natural archives' (the gold title's distinctive tokens), describing the event as rivers bursting their banks, the region as Spain and neighbouring southwestern Europe, and the evidence as bands of mud settled on lake bottoms. Pooled search on this final text (k=10, all four conditions, 23 distinct projects): FLOODARC ranks dense 1, hybrid 4, hybrid_rerank 4, lexical absent from the top 10 - BM25 no longer leads on title tokens, and the gold stays recoverable at dense rank 1. Adjudications - IN: 796752 FLOODARC (reconstructs the frequency and intensity of extreme river floods in Western Mediterranean/Iberian lake records and states the layer-identification protocol). OUT, all on their best chunk or an earlier full read: 101018321 TURBOMUD (paleoearthquakes from marine turbidites, Gulf of Cadiz); 804673 sEEIngDOM (dissolved organic matter); 759829 DISCOMPOSE (early-modern disaster communication and politics); 798529 LiguSTAR (Roman riparian landscape survey); 799544 GeoFodder (early animal husbandry geoarchaeology); 101024224 DMC-ReaDy (dormant microbes in lake sediment); 683018 PALEODEM (Iberian population history); 834329 SEDILAND (15-year instrumental sediment-transport records of modern river catchments); 863490 GyroSCoPe (river terraces, Patagonia and Tien Shan); 777167 BOUNCE (breast cancer); 101029581 WoodTiMe (post-medieval forest use); 703045 EPP-Am (Amazonian archaeology); 670518 Lost Frontiers (North Sea palaeolandscape); 883280 URBS (cathedral cities); 658863 SEDiLINK (mining pollution in estuarine cores); 811965 STINTS (skin tissue); 697066 JPM (district heating pipes); 706244 IRONLAKE (iron isotopes in Lago Fagnano laminae); 891464 SIFFT (solute isotopes, Guadeloupe); 898312 SmartHeart (cardiac assay); 835496 HEGS (flood probabilities from 20CR reanalysis and historical flood marks, no sediment); 101001835 STRADA (Adriatic-Danube transport simulation). Completeness sweep (run_sql, non-embedding, carried forward from the first-round draft because it keys on the unchanged concepts, not on the wording): (1) project.objective LIKE paleoflood/palaeoflood OR (flood AND lacustrine/lake sediment/sediment core/sedimentary archive/sedimentary record/natural archive) -> 1 row, 796752; (2) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults LIKE paleoflood/palaeoflood -> 1 row, 796752; (3) report_text sections LIKE flood AND (lake sediment/lacustrine/sediment core) -> 8 rows, of which the 7 non-gold were read and rejected (705633 SYNC, 703045 EPP-Am, 101029939 CROSSROADS, 805246 OldCO2NewArchives, 658863 SEDiLINK, 704822 MedCoRes, 802281 RISeR). Reference answer scope: the project used sediment cores and datasets that already existed at the studied sites (it is not stated to have drilled them), and the centuries-to-26000-years span is attributed to the flood records it analysed, which include compiled third-party reconstructions.

text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
reference_answer: Both projects treat protection against drying as something encoded in the sequence of proteins that never adopt a fixed structure, and both planned the same combination - large libraries of sequence variants, a score per variant, and machine learning to extract the rules - but each report records how far that plan actually got. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which under drying undergo glass-transition and gelation into vitrified solids that stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and aggregating, and planned computational analysis of known CAHS sequences, a designed library screened by a high-throughput survival assay, and machine-learning extraction of the features behind protective glass-transition; what its report describes as executed is an integrative analytical pipeline combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, through which it identified new protein sequences and features contributing to desiccation survival and uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance - the survival screen and the machine-learning step are not mentioned there. FLINDIP planned deep mutational scanning of tardigrade proteins essential for surviving complete desiccation, with cell libraries of hundreds of thousands of variants scored by competition assay; its report states that random-mutant libraries for the original target genes were built but the phenotype of Boothby et al 2017 could never be reproduced, so after the Covid-19 closure the work switched to desiccation-resistance proteins of the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family from Liu et al., 2019, whose repeat-rich sequences complicated synthesis and whose new libraries were near finishing preparation at grant end, and that the planned experimental work on intrinsically disordered proteins could not be completed by the end of the grant. FLINDIP's analysis half did deliver: the reusable pipeline was built and demonstrated on a Kondrashov lab dataset of mutants versus phenotype for four green fluorescent proteins (GFPs), published as Sommermeyer et al., 2022, whose finding was that mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design and that predictions are more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-49 (anhydrobiosis/desiccation survival). Candidate evidence re-executed as a drift check: the ILIKE probe over objective for tardigrad/anhydrobio/cryptobio/'desiccation tolerance' still returns 4 (734434 DRYNET, 747087 BIOSTASIS, 898203 FLINDIP, 838945 Desiccation Survival) and the plain label 'desiccation tolerance' over title-or-objective still returns 1. All four seeds were read in full. A first, broader wording ('molecules that let organisms lose nearly all their water and come back to life') pooled up RESIST (823746, resurrection plants) and the sweep added DRYSTORE (749537), which would have made |gold|=5-6 and an L3 survey, so the question was re-scoped to the shapeless-protein/sequence-determinant angle, which is what 838945 and 898203 share and the others do not. Adjudication of the 38 pooled candidates: 838945 IN - objective and report state that CAHS intrinsically disordered proteins in tardigrades vitrify under desiccation and that the project set out to find the sequence features that confer protection, and its report records an executed pipeline that identified new protein sequences and features contributing to desiccation survival; 898203 IN - objective states the project focuses on tardigrade proteins essential for surviving complete desiccation and measures the genotype-to-phenotype link of hundreds of thousands of variants by deep mutational scanning. 747087 BIOSTASIS OUT (seed, read in full) - comparative transcriptomics across tardigrade lineages to find key-player genes and pathways and gene regulation during entry to and recovery from desiccation; it names molecules implicated in the anhydrobiotic mechanism as a class but never asks which features of a protein's sequence confer protection. The other 36 pooled projects (795867 NovoFold, 894784 EMPHABIOSYS, 101030961 DEEPCONSTRUCT, 680375 PRESCREENARRAY, 647548 Protein Lego, 654719 lincPeptEvolDev, 695558 ProCovar, 787926 RIBOFOLD, 796969 GOKNOT, 803825 TransTempoFold, 706828 GSR, 867459 P-appetite, 101023654 SYN-CHARGE, 947709 HyDegronomics, 647458 MANGO, 726151 DeE-Nano, 798966 MemCHAPS, 648030 chemREPEAT, 715207 MMA, 669351 SGCR, 661247 FOLDASYNBIO, 705701 MolecularEVOLUTION, 101001169 PROT-STRUCT-DISEASE, 660083 MEMDYN, 101001394 tRNAslation, 844006 LEVERAGE mRNA, 884114 NaCRe, 766811 PeptIn, 798821 PPOM-PTT, 841193 inTECH, 823886 REFRACT, 964593 e-Prot, 862704 NextGenProteins, 891009 Collagen Origami, 642083 EURO-SEQUENCES, 833254 EPISWITCH) are OUT: their best chunks are about protein folding, design, aggregation, disease IDPs, polymers or food proteins, and none concerns survival of water loss. Completeness sweep (run_sql, no embeddings): (a) title-or-objective ILIKE over tardigrad/anhydrobio/cryptobio/desiccat/'resurrection plant'/rehydrat/'dry storage'/poikilohydr/rotifer/'LEA protein'/'late embryogenesis abundant'/xeroprotect returned 21 projects; the on-theme ones outside gold are DRYNET (734434) and DRYSTORE (749537), which pursue dry biobanking of cells and germplasm and name LEA proteins as xeroprotectants but never frame the work as finding the sequence features of unfolded proteins, RESIST (823746, resurrection plants, comparative plant genomics), RHEA (725998, bdelloid rotifer asexuality where desiccation appears only as a source of DNA breaks), plus clearly unrelated hits (3F-FutureFreshFruit fruit cuticle wax, SUBTOL seaweed submergence, iDAPT ice algae, CryoPlankton/MCRD cryopreservation, ASM nuclear-fuel dry storage, WoodTRACES); all OUT. (b) The intersection sweep - objective ILIKE ('intrinsically disordered'|'disordered protein'|'unstructured protein'|CAHS|'glass transition'|vitrif) AND (desicc|dry|dehydrat|'water loss'|anhydro) - returned exactly 838945 and 898203. (c) A wider list of all 51 projects whose objective mentions intrinsically disordered / disordered / unfolded proteins, trehalose or LEA proteins was inspected by title: none of the others concerns drying survival. Reference answer basis: written from both gold projects' objective AND report sections, keeping plan and executed work separate - FLINDIP's report records dropped target genes (Boothby et al 2017 phenotype not reproducible), a switch to LEA-family proteins from Liu et al., 2019 with libraries still in preparation at grant end, experimental work on intrinsically disordered proteins not completed, and the machine-learning pipeline demonstrated on the Kondrashov lab's four-GFP dataset (Sommermeyer et al., 2022); 838945's report records an executed pipeline of computational sequence analysis, NMR structural characterization, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, without mentioning the planned survival screen or machine-learning step. term_style=paraphrase: the question avoids every distinctive term the gold texts use - desiccation, intrinsically disordered, tardigrade, CAHS, glass-transition, deep mutational scanning, fitness landscape - and says 'no fixed folded structure', 'tiny animals', 'loss of virtually all their water'. The rank matrix agrees: neither gold project is found by lexical at k=20 (838945 dense 6 / hybrid 5 / hybrid_rerank 3; 898203 dense 12 / hybrid_rerank 11).

text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
reference_answer: Fourteen projects put a planted wetland bed of their own to work on water. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX reported constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material recovering nitrogen from source-separated urine, reaching NH4+ oxidation rates up to 284 mg N/L/d but only 43% N recovery; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands combined with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment as one of the natural-engineered combinations spread over its 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, which also cover bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm water retention and nutrient-recovery measures; DIVAGRI co-develops an artificial wetland with smallholders as one of seven bio-based technologies installed at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites in Sub-Saharan Africa, a water-saving technology alongside its sub-surface clay-based irrigation system; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-64 (constructed wetlands): 642190, 689450, 701542, 773351, 858375, 894525; the candidate's SQL (objective/title ILIKE '%constructed wetland%') re-executed in the drafting pass and still returns exactly those 6. MEMBERSHIP RULE (the axis, not the string): a project is IN when it installs, pilots or tests a planted wetland bed OF ITS OWN as a working unit handling a water stream - sewage, greywater, stormwater, groundwater, source-separated urine, farm drainage or runoff, or irrigation water - whatever word the project uses for it (constructed, artificial, treatment, METland, hybrid subsurface wetland). The wetland need NOT treat a named wastewater stream, and the literal word 'constructed' is not load-bearing. A project is OUT when it only studies, models, monitors, restores or writes about wetlands, or when a wetland it did not build is merely the setting or the motivation. Applied to the two agricultural cases in the same breath: 858375 WATERAGRI is IN - objective O4 'identify, develop and test affordable ... farm solutions such as ... farm constructed wetlands', report 'exploring nature-based methods (farm-constructed wetlands, controlled drainage, bio-inspired filters)' - a planted bed it develops and tests for on-farm water retention and nutrient recovery, not for sewage; 101000348 DIVAGRI is IN on exactly that rule - report summary 'Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites across the continent include a desalination greenhouse, artificial wetland, biogas digester, biochar kiln, a subsurface irrigation system, mobile biorefinery and intercropping', workPerformed 'Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers in the co-design phase ... All seven bio-based technologies will be installed at all pilot sites within the next few months'. Neither treats a named wastewater stream; both install a planted wetland bed of their own; they fall together. Other adjudications - IN: 642190 iMETland (METland units constructed and operated), 894525 ELECTRAMMOX (constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material, applied to N recovery from source-separated urine, 284 mg N/L/d oxidation, 43% recovery), 826244 ELECTRA ('solutions were relying on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands for wastewater treatment'), 689450 AquaNES (demonstrates CW plus engineered pre/post treatment), 773351 ZIRONITRO (a constructed wetland producing nitrate-free drinking water), 689242 INCOVER ('The sludge treatment wetland produced good quality soil conditioner'), 101003765 NICE (pilots 'designed, constructed & integrated', 'such as vertical gardens, constructed wetl&s, & rain gardens'), 776643 HYDROUSA ('Coupling anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands (CWs) and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection'), 821051 PAVITRA GANGA ('Constructed Wetlands + Technology: combining vertical subsurface flow CW with granular activated carbon and zeolite ... advancing from TRL 4 to TRL 6'), 861088 M2EX ('constructed wetlands (CWs) were employed to treat the resulting effluent'; 'ESR14 evaluated the potential of constructed wetlands (CWs) to recover/remove metals from wastewater/digestate'), 739732 INNOV ('Using constructed wetland technologies, alchemia-nova is developing indoor and outdoor plant-based applications, to treat such contaminated water for household reuse'), 820906 INDIA-H2O ('The treatment capacity has been validated in a small wetland construction and larger a larger scale solution has been constructed and will be installed and to treat the wastewater source at PDEU'). OUT: 701542 UMIC (seed rejected - names constructed wetlands only as context for what others propose; characterises U/Fe-organic-matter colloids in natural wetland environments and builds nothing), 660391 OPTWET (models optimal siting of restored/created wetlands in agricultural catchments), 101003527 MULTISOURCE (its ENTS/NBS pilots are never named as wetlands in stored text; its only wetland artefact is an open-access textbook on treatment wetlands, D4.5), 751692 BIRDBARRIER (reed beds as bird habitat), 786566 Mind4Stormwater (asset management of stormwater control measures built by others), 854782 M-NBS (modular phytoremediation sanitation unit, never described as a wetland), 689817 INNOQUA (lumbrifilter/daphniafilter sanitation), 704957 NANOREM (ZnO nanoparticle toxicity in wetland plants), 817155 Aqua Gratis (wetlands mentioned only as degraded water bodies), 647570 ESTUARIES and 890611 ORIGINSOFSCARCITY (wetland-system wording in estuarine morphodynamics and in groundwater politics respectively; no built bed), 642228 SUBSOL, 678168 NEURICE, 788009 IRMIDYN, 858378 EPSETECH; all other pooled candidates (EBBR, GREENER, SPRING, NOWELTIES, POWERSTEP, Water2REturn, MEMBio, Project O, FLEXBIO, MAT4TREAT, SMART, WaterLANDS, etc.) are reactor-based water treatment or wetland ecology with no built wetland bed in their text. Completeness sweeps (run_sql, non-embedding): (1) objective/title ILIKE '%constructed wetland%' -> 6; (2) that phrase family over objective+title+all report_text fields, including '%treatment wetland%', '%engineered wetland%', '%reed bed%' and the mangled '%constructed wetl&%' -> 15 projects, 12 gold and 3 rejected (UMIC, BIRDBARRIER, MULTISOURCE); (3) chunk-level: projects whose chunk text contains 'wetland' AND which anywhere mention wastewater/greywater/water treatment/effluent, minus those 15 -> 8 projects, of which only 820906 INDIA-H2O qualified; (4) objective probes for 'reed bed', 'planted filter', 'planted bed', 'phytodepuration', 'subsurface flow', 'vertical flow', 'macrophyte', 'green filter' -> nothing new; (5) added in the fix round to close the string-variant gap that hid DIVAGRI (sweep 3's second predicate excluded it): chunk-level '%artificial wetland%', '%man-made wetland%', '%wetland system%', '%wetland technolog%', '%wetland unit%', '%wetland pilot%' with NO water-vocabulary predicate -> 4 projects, of which 101000348 DIVAGRI is new and now gold, 739732 INNOV already gold, and 647570 ESTUARIES + 890611 ORIGINSOFSCARCITY rejected. POOLING SPLIT (the entry's derivation, reproducible in two independent halves): pooled_candidate_count 37 is the union of the four conditions' top-20 for the recorded question text; 8 of the gold set were accepted out of that pool (pooling_evidence.accepted_from_pool: 642190 iMETland lex 1/dense 1/hyb 1/rerank 1, 689450 AquaNES 7/3/4/2, 826244 ELECTRA 4/2/3/6, 894525 ELECTRAMMOX 2/5/2/3, 689242 INCOVER 3/-/6/10, 101003765 NICE 10/4/5/4, 821051 PAVITRA GANGA 5/-/16/5, 861088 M2EX -/8/11/7), 29 pooled candidates were rejected, and 6 further gold members were added by reading and by the non-embedding sweeps, reached by no condition at k=20 (pooling_evidence.accepted_by_reading: 773351 ZIRONITRO, 739732 INNOV, 776643 HYDROUSA, 820906 INDIA-H2O, 858375 WATERAGRI, 101000348 DIVAGRI). Gold is the true satisfying set, not what retrieval found; the low uniform recall on this cell is a measurement about retrieval, and the 8 retrieved members still separate the conditions (INCOVER and PAVITRA GANGA null on dense, M2EX null on lexical). term_style exact-term: the question reuses the projects' own vocabulary - 'constructed wetland', 'METland', 'subsurface flow', 'sludge treatment wetland'; the rank matrix agrees, lexical ranking iMETland 1, ELECTRAMMOX 2, INCOVER 3, ELECTRA 4, PAVITRA GANGA 5, AquaNES 7, NICE 10.
